mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of >0.5% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) above 0.3 percentage points over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > 0.3pp over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.3pp over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter, combined with a concurrent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST), signals a consumption-led recovery, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +1% qoq above trend AND HOUST > +5% m-o-m
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 exceeds trend by >1% qoq and HOUST rises by >5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows by >0.5% m-o-m for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for two consecutive months, regardless of regime, signals weakening consumer demand and is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines by more than 1% for two consecutive months.
